Ventilation balancing is the process of commissioning an air‐handling or mechanical ventilation system so that each supply and exhaust outlet delivers exactly the intended airflow rate. In practice it involves measuring the airflow in each duct or diffuser, then adjusting dampers or fan speeds until the system is “balanced.”  

Energy‐performance impacts of proper ventilation balancing  
1. Reduced heating and cooling loads  
   • Prevents over-ventilation, which otherwise forces the heating or cooling plant to condition more outdoor air than needed.  
   • Improves heat‐recovery efficiency in balanced ventilation systems (e.g. HRV/ERV units), so you reclaim more heat in winter (or coolth in summer) from the exhaust air stream.  

2. Lower fan power consumption  
   • Avoids excessive static pressures and fan speeds that waste electricity.
